title: The Best Gengar Cards to Collect — Fossil to Mega Gengar ex, Raw to PSA 10, Dated Sold Prices | Gengar's Collector's Desk
description: Gengar picks his own true collectibles: Fossil Gengar (1st Edition and Unlimited), Dark Gengar from Neo Destiny, the Skyridge pair, Gengar & Mimikyu GX, Mega Gengar ex from Ascended Heroes, the 30th Celebration Gengar ex and an under-$20 shelf — each with dated raw, PSA 9, PSA 10 and TAG 10 sold prices and eBay links.
keywords: best gengar cards, gengar cards to collect, fossil gengar, dark gengar neo destiny, gengar mimikyu gx, mega gengar ex, most valuable gengar cards, gengar card collection
intro: Yes, this is my own desk. I'm biased, and I'm also right: Gengar has had a holo in nearly every era that mattered, the art has always been a little mean, and the grades on the vintage ones are brutally hard. These are the ones that belong in a collection, from a $4 holo to a Skyridge slab that sells for the price of a car.
narratorNote: A note on the obvious conflict of interest: I'm a ghost picking ghost cards. The prices are not mine, though. Every number is a dated sold price from the same index data that feeds the card pages, and every print below is searched by its exact set and number. I grin at the cards I like. I don't tell you to buy them.

shelves.label: The grails
shelves.blurb: Wizards-era Gengar holos. One print run each, dark art, and PSA 10s that almost never come up — which is why they sell the way they do when they do.

entries.title: Fossil Gengar #5 (1999)
entries.why: The original. Fossil was the third English set, the first with Gengar in it, and this holo is the card most of us saw first. The 1st Edition print is the serious one; the Unlimited is the same art for a tenth of the money raw, and the PSA 10 gap between them is where the whole vintage market lives.

entries.title: Dark Gengar, Neo Destiny #6 (2002)
entries.why: Neo Destiny gave the Dark Pokémon a second run and this Gengar holo is the best of them: a nastier version of an already nasty Pokémon, on a holo from the last Neo set. The 1st Edition is a real auction card now; the Unlimited is where a collector can still find one raw.

entries.title: Skyridge Gengar H9 and #10 (2003)
entries.why: Skyridge was Wizards of the Coast's last Pokémon set, with a single print run, and it printed Gengar twice: the H9 holo and the #10 non-holo rare. The holo trades almost only graded, which is why there is no clean raw price on it. The #10 is the collector's way in to the same set and the same art.

shelves.label: The centerpieces
shelves.blurb: The modern Gengars that already trade like collectibles — a chase slot in their set, art people recognise across the room, a graded market we can mark every week.

entries.title: Mega Gengar ex, Ascended Heroes (2026)
entries.why: The Special Illustration Rare #284 is the heaviest card in our whole Ascended Heroes index — a 2026 set where a Gengar outweighs the Pikachu and the Charizard. That does not happen often. The #269 is the regular ex art for a collector who wants the Mega without the SIR price.

entries.title: Gengar & Mimikyu GX, Team Up (2019)
entries.why: The Tag Team era's Gengar, printed four ways in Team Up: the regular #53, the full art #164, the alternate art #165 and the rainbow #186. The #165 alternate art is the one collectors mean when they say this card, and it has become one of the most expensive Sun & Moon cards outright.
entries.note: Searches for this card need the phrase Tag Team kept in, so the graded links here use the Team Up rule from our card pages rather than the usual TAG-slab filter.

entries.title: Gengar ex #154, 30th Celebration (2026)
entries.why: The 30th Celebration set's Gengar ex, released this September. Too new for a graded mark that meets our rule, so the ladder shows what it can and nothing it can't. The #94 is the set's regular Gengar.

shelves.label: The starter shelf
shelves.blurb: Gengars for under $20 raw. Real cards from real sets, not placeholders.

entries.title: Fossil Gengar #20 (1999)
entries.why: The non-holo print of the Fossil Gengar, same 1999 art without the foil. The cheapest Wizards-era Gengar there is, and still a card a PSA 10 turns into real money.

entries.title: Gengar #94, Scarlet & Violet 151 (2023)
entries.why: The 151 set's Gengar, numbered by Pokédex. A few dollars raw, and the first Gengar a lot of kids pulled this decade.

entries.title: Gengar ex #90, 30th Celebration (2026)
entries.why: The regular-art Gengar ex from the 30th set, for a collector who wants this year's Gengar without the #154 price.

collectingNotes.p: Vintage Gengar holos are dark cards, and dark cards show every scratch and every white edge under a grader's light. That is a large part of why a Fossil or Neo Destiny Gengar in a PSA 10 sells for so many multiples of raw, and why a raw copy's condition matters more here than on a bright card.

collectingNotes.h: 1st Edition and Unlimited are different cards
collectingNotes.p: Fossil and Neo Destiny each exist as a 1st Edition print and an Unlimited print with separate PSA labels, separate population reports and separate price histories. Our indices track them as separate cards and every link on this page searches for the exact print on the row.

A plain search for TAG-graded Gengar cards pulls in every Gengar & Mimikyu TAG TEAM listing. Our card pages use a slab phrase and drop the Tag Team words for every set except Team Up itself; the links here follow the same rule.

PSA 10 is the hobby's price reference. TAG grades by machine-measured imaging with human review and publishes a full defect report for every card, which is why we link TAG slabs beside PSA on every row. We think measured grading is where the hobby is heading — our view, not a price claim. How TAG grading works →
